definitions.explanation: A pattern of irregular spots or patches of different colors. Describes something with an uneven mix of colors or shades.
Used figuratively to describe something that is inconsistent or uneven in quality, distribution, or degree.

examples.japanese: まだら⟦{模様|もよう}→模様：03635_moyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
⟦{壁|かべ}→壁：01290_kabe⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧まだら⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{汚|よご}れている→汚れる：01293_yogoreru⟧。
examples.english: The wall is stained in patches.

examples.japanese: ⟦{白|しろ}→白：13854_shiro⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{茶色|ちゃいろ}→茶色：02915_chairo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧まだら⟦{模様|もよう}→模様：03635_moyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子犬|こいぬ}→子犬：19393_koinu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飼|か}っている→飼う：08151_kau⟧。
examples.english: I have a puppy with a white and brown spotted pattern.

examples.japanese: ⟦{記憶|きおく}→記憶：00234_kioku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧まだらだ。
⟦{出席|しゅっせき}→出席：02084_shusseki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧まだらになっている。
⟦{雪|ゆき}→雪：00584_yuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧まだら⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{残|のこ}っている→残る：01187_nokoru⟧⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{景色|けしき}→景色：01395_keshiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{美|うつく}しかった→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧。
examples.english: The mountain scenery with snow remaining in patches was beautiful.

notes:
Can be written in kanji as {斑|まだら}, but the kana form is more common. Functions as a noun and as a modifier (まだら⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ or まだらな). The word can also be used adverbially with ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (まだら⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- まだら⟦{模様|もよう}→模様：03635_moyou⟧ — mottled/spotted pattern
- まだら⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まる→染まる：04254_somaru⟧ — to be dyed unevenly
- ⟦{記憶|きおく}→記憶：00234_kioku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧まだら — patchy memory
- まだら⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{残|のこ}る→残る：01187_nokoru⟧ — to remain in patches

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{縞|しま}→縞：27905_shima⟧ — stripes; a regular pattern of parallel lines, unlike the irregular spots of まだら
- ⟦{水玉|みずたま}→水玉：16173_mizutama⟧ — polka dots; regular, uniform round spots, unlike the irregular patches of まだら
- ぶち — patches of color on an animal's coat; similar to まだら but used almost exclusively for animal markings
- むら — unevenness, inconsistency; overlaps with sense 2 but focuses on quality variation rather than visual pattern
